summary.headline: Fiem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.6% to INR769.9 crore with EBITDA margin steady at 13.5%; FY27 4-wheeler ramp pushed out to FY28.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 sales grew 18.62% YoY to INR769.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR104.06 crore at a 13.5% margin, versus 13.46% a year ago. PAT increased 16.31% to INR65.19 crore. Management said raw material and employee cost increases will be passed on with a lag over the next few quarters, and reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and about 14% EBITDA margin. The main negative was the 4-wheeler lighting ramp, which management now expects to slip into FY28 from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 13.46% YoY; about 130 bps QoQ compression as stated by an analyst

financial_highlights.metric: LED share of automotive lighting revenue

financial_highlights.change: Analyst figure; company has no debt per analyst

segments.name: 2-wheeler lighting
segments.commentary: Core growth engine. Management says volumes are in line with TVS, Honda and Suzuki; Yamaha lagged, with exports up only 2-3% against domestic up 40-50% per an analyst. Industry production reached 7.25 million units in Q1, about 22.8% growth per management.

segments.name: EV lighting
segments.commentary: EV share of 2-wheeler volume is above 9%, up from about 6% a year ago. Supplies commenced for Ather Konarc (sole supplier on the new model), River RX02 and Royal Enfield EV Flying Flea. Hero Vida lamps for its Andhra Pradesh plant will ship from Hosur from next quarter.

segments.name: 4-wheeler lighting
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of revenue. Management now expects FY27 to stay at a similar level, with meaningful scale-up pushed to FY28 because customer conversion is taking longer. Mahindra supplies are scaling as planned; Force Motors and other OEM development is ongoing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 15-20%, unchanged; management said this holds for the years to come until a significant move into another business.
EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for the full year; Q1 carried cost increases in employee cost and raw materials.
Raw material cost increase (about 80 bps of the margin impact per management) expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters.
Employee cost run-rate expected to stay at the Q1 level for the next three quarters after the minimum wage revision (Haryana first, about 35% increase there, other states following).
FY27 capex target about INR100 crore, versus about INR110 crore in FY26; most of it for Hosur (EV capacity for TVS and others), some at Tapukara.
4-wheeler lighting revenue for FY27 now expected at about 2.5% of revenue, versus the earlier INR100-150 crore indication; the ramp shifts to FY28.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR41.15 crore; FY27 target about INR100 crore, largely Hosur (Kelamangalam and Thally Road) for EV capacity.
Customers expanding: TVS 2-wheeler capacity 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by year-end; Hero Vida capacity 15,000 to 45,000 units per month.
Hands-off detection POC built and shown to almost all customers; light control module (LCM) expected to launch with 2-3 customers soon.
In-house EMI/EMC lab supports faster validation and shorter development time.
demand_pricing: Industry: record Q1 2-wheeler volume of 7.25 million units, supported by GST rationalisation, retail financing and rural demand; exports and EVs grew faster.
Management says wallet share with top customers is same or better; more than 100 models are with Fiem across customers.
Mercedes: samples submitted, with 1.5-2 years of vehicle-level testing before an RFQ/RFI for mass production.
Ambient lighting using optical fibre: technology not yet uniform; business expected to be cracked in about a year with customers.
LED share of automotive lighting at 63%; management expects new models to move to LED and targets about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY27 4-wheeler lighting guidance (INR100-150 crore in the prior quarter) cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is pushed out by about two quarters, with FY27 slightly lower and 4-wheeler at about 2.5% of revenue. Orders are lumpy and conversion cycles with customers are longer.

qa_highlights.question: How will LED penetration move in 2-wheeler lighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new models are coming with LEDs only and it expects about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months. It does not expect 100% because older models and aftermarket demand will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Yamaha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Yamaha to be flat to growing for the year. Exports were weak on the cycle of European and US demand; domestic models such as R15, Aerox and XSR were slower in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and cost pass-through outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 14% EBITDA margin for FY27. Raw material cost increases are expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters; the employee cost run-rate should hold for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is capital allocation given about INR280 crore cash and no debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited organic and inorganic opportunities, plus possible future 4-wheeler and electronics capex. It will fund capex from internal accruals and would raise debt if needed for a larger opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company disclose wallet share by customer and segment?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst asked for annual wallet share disclosure by segment. Management declined to share it in advance, citing customer confidentiality, and said it will announce models after customer launches.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler ramp has slipped again; FY28 is now the earliest meaningful scale-up, and analysts questioned competitive share gains.
Yamaha exports and domestic models slowed in Q1; management expects recovery but gave no quarterly targets.
Input cost and rupee pressure: pass-through has a lag, so margin in the next 1-2 quarters depends on recovery.
Employee cost step-up from minimum wage revisions across states, which management expects to persist for the next three quarters.
Hands-off detection and LCM remain at POC or pre-launch stage with no order value disclosed; ambient lighting timing is about a year away.
Analysts asked about share loss at top customers; management did not give a quantified wallet share figure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on 2-wheeler and EV demand and the festive outlook, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the 4-wheeler timeline and on customer-level market share. Management repeatedly declined to give specifics on new products and wallet share.
key_quotes: So the margin guidance for the year is around 14%.
We look at overall revenue guidance of around 15% to 20%.
But next year onwards, we should see some significant increase.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%), backed by Q1 revenue growth of 18.6% and an active Hosur EV capacity build (~INR100 crore FY27 capex), though the 4-wheeler ramp slips to FY28 and utilisation is not disclosed.
